while the intro flag zpa_BD is set plays a random tick on voice 2 one frame in three (a counter at a_980B runs 1, 2, 3: the tick starts on 1 and the gate closes on 3) and, every frame, rotates the eight bytes at $33E0 so the cover character animates
calls the random reveal, then draws every cell of the cave in order into the scroll buffer and fills the buffer edges

builds one pixel row Y of Rockford's tile for the current phase, X being 16 times the phase plus Y: the head characters $4C and $4D ($3260, $3268) and the feet $5C and $5D ($32E0, $32E8). Moving (zpa_8B not $0F) it clears zpa_BE and zpa_BF and copies from $64E8/$64F0 and $6568/$6570 when facing left (zpa_98 not zero), or $65E8/$65F0 and $6668/$6670 when facing right. Standing still (zpa_8B = $0F) the head comes from the blink table $63E8/$63F0 while zpa_BF is set, else from characters $42 and $43, and the feet from the tap table $6468/$6470 while zpa_BE is set, else from $52 and $53; when X is 0, once per cycle of eight phases, zpa_BF is set with one chance in four and zpa_BE toggled with one chance in sixteen

builds the animated characters of the current phase zpa_C0 into the character set: the diamond (char $48 at $3240) and Rockford always, and the firefly (bit 0 of the mask zpf_FF, char $64 at $3320), butterfly (bit 1, char $20 at $3100) and amoeba (bit 2, char $40 at $3200) sets only when the cave uses them
while the flash counter zpa_A5 runs turns the background and border colours white, and black when it ends

once a frame sets the SID volume to 15 and, unless paused (zpa_9B), plays what the game asked for: on voice 3 the effect from sid_voice3_regs for $21 frames while zpa_D8 is set (the end of the intro countdown and the quota), otherwise the amoeba hum while play is on and the amoeba found room in the last pass (zpa_43), else silence unless the magic wall is active; on voice 1, on frames where a_980F AND a_9878 is zero, the sound buffered at $987D when a_980D counts a request, or else its sustain level halved until it is zero; then, outside the intro (zpa_BD), counts the lockout a_9811 down and plays the step and dig notes from a_9808 on voice 2, but not while a_980D bit 7 (set by the low-time beep) or a_9811 is set ($7DD7-$7DE4)

copies the eight bytes of character $4E, the brick wall's, from $3270 into the magic wall's four characters $22, $23, $32 and $33 ($3110, $3118, $3190, $3198), so the magic wall looks like brick: at the start of a cave ($8294) and when the wall runs out ($7E84)

while the magic wall is active plays a random note on voice 3 on alternate frames and copies eight bytes from $3360 plus (zpa_C0 AND $1F), one of four frames at $3360-$337F, into each of the magic wall's four characters $22, $23, $32 and $33 ($3110, $3118, $3190, $3198), animating the wall
runs the magic wall animation while it is active (zpa_8D = 1) and ends it at state 2
advances the animation phase zpa_C0 by 8 modulo $40, builds the new frames and runs the magic wall animation

counts frames in zpa_8E and, every 60 ($3C), seconds in zpa_8F while (zpa_9B EOR 1) AND zpa_8D is 1 ($7E9F-$7EA5): the magic wall is active (zpa_8D = 1) and zpa_9B is 0 or 2. So the count stops while zpa_9B is 1, at the start of a pause ($8110) and at the end of a cave ($8C44), but goes on while pause_screen holds zpa_9B at 2 ($80D7) for the rest of a pause. When the seconds equal the cave header byte at $2401 sets zpa_8D to 2, the wall expired

the once-per-frame job started from the interrupt when zpa_A7 is zero: flash, intro effects, magic wall timer, clock, sound, scrolling, then on every second frame the screen copy routine, on the others it swaps the double-buffer flag

256 bytes of code that are copied to $9E00 at start and run from there: they work out the scroll buffer and screen addresses for the current screen base zpa_D6/D7 and copy rows of the scroll buffer into the screen; the unrolled loads show $5000 and $0C50 because the real operands are patched in at $9E00
the second 256-byte block of code copied to $9F00: the remainder of the screen copy routine, ending with a call to animation_step and to sparkle_step while the glisten counter runs

makes one random cell of the starting cave: takes a random byte from the generator in zpa_3E/3F (cave_random_step), and stores in the cell at offset $29 from zpp_32 the code at $2418+Y for the last Y of 0 to 3 whose threshold at $241C+Y is above that byte, else dirt (1). The codes and thresholds are header bytes 24-27 and 28-31: space, boulder and diamond in most caves, but also fireflies ($08, caves 2, 7, 8, 11 and 15) and brick wall ($02, cave 3)
fills the cave's rows 1 to 21 (21 rows of 40; row 0 is left alone) with build_cave_cell
per-level delay counts loaded into zpa_9C, 12, 6, 3, 1 and 0
busy-waits for zpa_9C times a short loop; used to slow a pass on the easy levels
writes 8 and then 0 to the control register of SID voice 1 ($D404), so the gate closes
the same for voice 2 ($D40B)
the same for voice 3 ($D412)
silences the three voices (silence_voice_1 to silence_voice_3) and writes $4F to $D418: master volume 15 in the low nibble, $4 in the filter bits of the high nibble
a busy loop of about 128 passes of 256 for timing pauses
four times delay_short

waits $90 passes of a 256-step loop that tests the key flag zpa_FC, about 480,000 cycles, and returns at once when zpa_FC is $EF, the SPACE key (row 7, column 4); pause_screen's delay between flashes, so that SPACE ends the pause without waiting
shows the pause text on the status line and flashes it until the space-bar flag zpa_FC says to carry on

handles the keyboard flags at the end of each update pass ($81D2), so a pass that a boulder landing on the magic wall cuts short ($7775) skips it: SPACE ($EF in zpa_FC) stops play (zpa_94 = 0), silences the sound, sets the pause flag zpa_9B and runs pause_screen, then clears zpa_9B and sets zpa_94 back to 1; RUN/STOP ($7F in zpa_FC), once the intro countdown zpa_95 has reached zero, stops play and sets zpa_97 to 2, ending the cave; then clears zpa_FC; F1 ($EF in zpa_FB) restarts the whole program at $8E6A

after the update pass records whether the amoeba found room to grow (zpf_42 into zpa_43), clearing the growth flag zpa_8C when it had room before and none now, and copies the amoeba count a_9802 to a_9803

runs read_fire; when zpa_96 is $10, so no Rockford has been handled for 16 passes (update_pass counts it up to $10 at $8186-$818C, rockford_handler clears it at $7648), the fire button is pressed (zpa_B8 = 0) and the seconds counter zpa_AF (second_tick, $747B) is not zero, sets zpa_97 to 2 and so ends the cave: once Rockford is gone, fire moves on

one pass over the cave, run again and again by play_loop ($8C92) and once per script step by demo_play ($8CDE): counts zpa_96 up to $10, runs check_restart_fire and end_of_pass, then walks every column of rows 1 to 21 (rows 1 to 14 in caves 17 to 20, zpp_02 at $8171-$817D) with the handled cell at offset $29 from zpp_32; looks the cell's object up in the table of handlers at $5F68 and jumps to the handler when its high byte is not zero; the handlers end at end_of_object ($81AD), which applies the remap table at $5EE8 to the cell at offset 0 from zpp_32, one row up and one column left of the handled cell, so the 'handled' object codes are turned back one row and one column behind the scan, and goes on to the next cell

applies the remap table at $5EE8 to the cell at offset 0 from zpp_32 (Y = 0), one row up and one column left of the handled cell at offset $29, so the 'handled' codes are turned back one row and one column behind the scan, after it has passed them; then advances zpp_32 to the next cell and column and, after each row, delays on the easy levels (short_delay); after the last row runs pause_and_restart_keys
the weights 0, 0, 1 added by the decimal conversion
converts the count in zpa_C6 into three decimal digits in zpf_C3-C5 by adding the weights at $81D6 with carry, counting zpa_C6 down

the operand ($E9) of the branch at $81FB in binary_to_decimal, which repeats the decimal conversion loop at $81E6 until the count in zpa_C6 reaches zero; two bytes before the cave order table at $81FE, with the RTS at $81FD between. next_cave reads the table through this address ($8BDC, LDA $81FC,X with X twice the cave number), so cave 1's next cave is at $81FE; load_cave_data ($8230) and show_cave_name ($83A2) read the second byte of each entry through $81FD the same way

two bytes per cave number, 1 to 20 ($81FE-$8225): the cave that follows it (read by next_cave through $81FC plus twice the cave number) and a flag that is 1 when the cave itself is an intermission, caves 17 to 20 (read through $81FD plus twice the cave number by load_cave_data and show_cave_name). The order is A, B, C, D, then intermission 17, E to H, 18, I to L, 19, M to P, 20; the value $15 after cave 20 ends a round: next_cave goes back to cave 1 and raises the level, unless it is level 5 already

when the cave number zpa_5D has changed copies the $F0-byte description of the cave (at $582E plus the offset in the table at $5804) into $2400, then takes the random seed for the level, sets the two multicolour registers from $2413/$2414 and fills colour RAM from $2415

clears the cave's play variables (among them the magic wall state and its frame and second counts zpa_8D-zpa_8F, the quota flag zpa_90, the seconds zpa_AF and frames zpa_AE, zpa_96, zpa_97 and the pause flag zpa_9B) and restores the magic wall characters; sets the delay for the level, the time ($240E+level) in zpa_C7 and the three time digits, the diamonds needed ($2409+level), the two values of a diamond ($2402 before the quota, $2403 after), clears the diamond count, sets zpa_8C and the intro flag zpa_93 to 1 and the intro delay zpa_95 (4; 6 for two players on one joystick; one more in cave 2); sets the amoeba rate zpa_9A to $7F and the object mask zpf_FF to 7, then for caves 1 to 16 from the table at $8740, indexed by the cave number minus one
draws the GAME OVER line at $6F8C and waits

waits $75 x $80 passes of a loop that reads the fire button with read_fire_button ($6F03), about 720,000 cycles without the interrupt's share, and returns early when fire is pressed. It reads the fire bit only, not the keyboard; the port is joystick 1 unless the two-joystick flag zpa_A4 is set and the player value is 1: zpa_9D after an intermission (zpa_A6 set), its opposite otherwise

flashes OUT OF TIME on the status row: draws the 20 codes at $6FB4 (four spaces and OUT OF TIME, from text_status_template), waits once with wait_for_fire, draws the status row saved at $9862 and waits three times more; repeats until a round ends with the fire button pressed (zpa_B8 = 0) or for 20 rounds (a_9806), after which it clears zpa_B8 itself. end_of_cave calls it when the time has run out ($83C6-$83D5)

before the next cave reads that cave's intermission flag from the order table ($81FD plus twice zpa_5D) into zpa_A6; for an intermission draws BONUS LIFE ($6FC8) on the status row and runs add_life, which gives a man more and the glisten effect unless the player already has nine ($73D3); otherwise draws the status line from $984E (player, men, cave and level)

after a cave or the demonstration: when the seconds gone zpa_AF equal the cave's time zpa_C7, the time has run out, stops play (zpa_94 = 0), stores $10 at $0C18 and runs show_out_of_time, which flashes OUT OF TIME until fire or for 20 rounds; then, when the game is over (zpa_A0), stops play, shows GAME OVER and sets the magic wall state zpa_8D to 2 (magic_wall_animation then restores the wall's characters and silences voice 3, $7E80-$7E8C), otherwise, unless the cave number zpa_5D is 0, runs show_cave_name for the next cave; then sets zpa_BD, silences the sound, wipes the cave with scatter_cover and fill_screen_buffer, and after a game over waits with delay_long
the map-screen row start addresses, $0800 plus $28 per row, 24 entries, words from $0800 to $0B98

the high bytes of row_address_table: row_pointer ($8436) reads the low byte at $8406 and the high byte here at $8407, each plus twice the row, from 24 little-endian words $0800 to $0B98 in steps of $28; a cave description's row y gives $0800 + 40y, so y = 2 is the map's first row at $0850
turns the row zpa_DC and column zpa_DB of a cave-description object into the address zpa_3A/3B in the map
stores the object in zpa_DA in the map cell addressed by the row and column of the current cave description object
the 16-bit steps for the eight directions of cave-description lines
the rest of the eight direction steps, 16-bit words such as -1, 1, -40 and 40 for the neighbours of a map cell, read by the line routine at $8464
stores the object zpa_DA in zpa_C8 cells along the direction in A starting at the cell addressed by zpa_3A/3B
draws a line object of the cave description: a start cell, a length and a direction
fills a rectangle of width zpa_DD and height zpa_DF with object zpa_DA
draws the filled rectangle, then the object zpa_E0 inside it
draws the four sides of a rectangle with object zpa_DA
advances Y over the bytes of the current cave description object
adds two to the byte index in Y and runs the routine at $8507 that adds three more and stores it in zpa_CB, so one cave-object record is stepped over
adds one to Y and then steps over the rest of the record through the routine at $850D

walks the cave description list from $2420: each record starts with a code (top two bits: 00 single point, 40 line, 80 filled rectangle with an inner fill, C0 outline rectangle; low six bits the object); stops at the end byte $FF; for object $25 (the entrance) it also records Rockford's column zpa_44 and row zpa_45

unless the logo flag zpa_A3 is set, writes the two digits of the title's menu line 1 PLAYER 1 JOYSTICK (row 22 of the title screen at $0800): the number of players, zpa_9E + 1, at $0B70/$0B71, and the number of joysticks, zpa_A4 + 1, at $0B84/$0B85, each as the pair code, code + $34
draws a steel wall ($07) frame around the 40 by 22 cave

builds the title and menu screen into the map at $0828 and the lines of text at $0AF8-$0B98 from the tables at $6F14-$7004 (on one path the lines at $0B20 and $0B48 instead come from the score buffers at $9812 and $9826) and the map part from the title templates at $66E8-$68E7

the table of SID frequency words the title music reads: music_step takes the low byte at $86CA and the high byte at $86CB, each plus twice the note number ($8780-$8789, $8791-$879A). Notes 0-9 would fall on the last instructions of build_menu_screen at $86CA-$86DD, but the tune uses notes 15 to 58 only; notes 10 to 58 are the 49 words at $86DE-$873F, rising from $02DC to $2DC0
the high byte of each frequency word in the table at $86CA, read at the same index as the low byte

the SID frequency words of notes 10 to 58 of the note table that starts at $86CA: 49 little-endian words rising from $02DC to $2DC0, which music_step reads through $86CA and $86CB plus twice the note number ($8780-$879A); the title tune uses notes 15 to 58. The cave offsets are elsewhere, the 20 words at $5806-$582D

one byte for each of caves 1 to 16, loaded into zpf_FF by start_cave_variables from $8740 + the cave number - 1 ($8329-$8333); caves 17 to 20 keep the mask 7, so the last four bytes ($8750-$8753) are never read. Bit 0 the cave has fireflies, bit 1 butterflies, bit 2 (a value of 4 or more) the amoeba: build_animation_frames, every second frame, rebuilds only those creatures' animated characters

works on every other call, when zpa_C1 is odd (title_step calls it twice a frame). When a_980C is $A0 it gates voices 1 and 2 off, sets voice 2's envelope to $A8/$A8 and plays the next pair of the title tune: voice 1's note from $5FE9 and voice 2's from $5FE8 plus a_9800, which steps by two, looked up in the note table at $86CA; a_9801 counts the tune's passes when a_9800 wraps. On every working call it sets voice 1's sustain from a_980C (11, 11, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5 for $A0 to $A7), gates both voices on with $11, and steps a_980C from $A0 to $A7 and round (ADC #1, AND #$A7), so a new pair starts once every eight working calls, eight frames. With the demo flag zpa_A2 set, when a_9801 reaches 2 sets b_CD, which ends menu_loop and starts the demonstration
ORs the eight bytes at $2030 and $2038 with $2000 into $2048 and $2050, building the cycling colour characters

the title's step, run by the raster interrupt on each of its two interrupts a frame (lines $28 and $CA) while zpa_CE is 1: the first call after build_title_screen clears zpa_CF only sets zpa_CF to 1; after that counts zpa_C1 1, 2, 3, 0, and when it wraps (every fourth call, every second frame) rotates the colour table and rebuilds the colour characters; calls music_step on every call, which works when zpa_C1 is odd

decodes the F3 key at the title (zpa_FB = $DF): cycles zpa_D0 through one player, two players with one joystick and two players with two joysticks, updates the player and joystick flags zpa_9E and zpa_A4 and redraws the menu line

at the title reads joystick 1: down and up lower and raise the level zpa_5E within 0 to 4 (shown as 1 to 5: the digit is zpa_5E + $11), and moving up to level 4 sets the cave back to A ($886C-$8874); left steps the cave zpa_5D down by four while it is 5 or more, and right steps it up by four while it is below $0D and only at levels 1 to 3 ($888E-$8892), so the caves offered are A, E, I and M, and at levels 4 and 5 only A. Any direction clears the demo timer a_9801. Unless the logo flag zpa_A3 is set, redraws the cave letter at $0BA6 and the level digit at $0BBA on the menu line; then waits with delay_short

the title menu loop: each time round runs menu_keys (F3) and menu_cave_select (joystick 1). While the logo flag zpa_A3 is set it waits for F1 ($EF in zpa_FB), which sets zpa_CC, rebuilds the screen with the credit lines and clears zpa_A3 ($8916); once zpa_A3 is clear it colours and redraws the menu digits and reads the fire button on port 1 ($6F0C), which clears the demo flag zpa_A2 and sets b_CD. Loops until b_CD is set: by fire, to play, or by music_step after two passes of the tune with zpa_A2 still set, to the demonstration

copies the eight bytes of character $0B at $2058 into character 0 at $2000 (the pattern rotate_colour_table turns), sets cave 1 and the demo flag zpa_A2, and runs menu_loop, which returns when b_CD is set; then sets zpa_BD and zpa_C2, loads the VIC table for the demonstration and play from $89A4 into zpa_54-5B and sets zpa_CE to 0, play mode, so the interrupt runs frame_update from now on; clears zpa_C1 and the key flags zpa_FB and zpa_FC and silences the sound; with the demo flag still set takes level 1 and cave 1; writes the men digit (3), the cave letter and the level digit into the status line at $984E, sets zpa_95 to $13 and clears zpa_94, draws the status line on the status row and sets zpa_97 to 2
the border, background and extra background colours for the title screen, written to $D020-$D024

the eight bytes start_interrupts loads into zpa_54-5B ($8E43) for the title screens, before build_title_screen and menu_loop: for each of the two raster regions a $D011, a $D016 and a $D018 value and the line of the next interrupt. The interrupt at line $28 sets text on the screen at $0800 with the text set at $2000 ($1B, $18, $28) and asks for line $CA; the one at $CA sets multicolour bitmap mode ($3B) with the bitmap at $2000, which shows the logo in its last six rows ($37C0-$3F3F), and asks for line $28. While zpa_A3 is 0 the interrupt puts $1B in zpa_54, so the lower region stays text and the logo is not shown ($8A6C-$8A72)

the eight bytes title_setup loads into zpa_54-5B ($894B), after menu_loop and before it sets zpa_CE to 0, for the demonstration and play: the interrupt at line $28 shows the status row from the screen at $0C00 with the text set at $2000 ($D011 $1B, $D016 $18, $D018 $38) and asks for line $3B; the one at $3B shows the cave in multicolour, 38 columns, from the screen at $0C00 with the tile set at $3000 ($D011 $10, $D016 $10, $D018 $3C) and asks for line $28. In play the scroll steps rewrite zpa_54 and zpa_56 ($78AA, $792D) and frame_update zpa_58 ($7EE5), switching the cave between the screens at $0C00 and $2C00

builds the title screen with build_menu_screen; while the logo flag zpa_A3 is set fills $0AF8-$0BE7, the screen cells under the logo, with $6E; clears b_CD; sets $D018 to $28 (screen $0800, text set $2000) and $D020-$D024 from title_colours; fills colour RAM with colour 9 and then $DB01-$DBFF with colour 1 (the same loop also stores 1 in $DC00); clears zpa_CF and sets zpa_CE to 1, title mode; waits until the interrupt's title_step sets zpa_CF, then clears the music and sound state ($9800, $9801, $9808, $9809, $980B, $980E, $980F, $9811)

the game's interrupt: alternates between the two screen regions by writing the VIC registers from the tables at zpa_54-5B, scans the keyboard rows for F1, F3, SPACE and RUN/STOP with a two-read debounce into zpa_FB-FE, then at the title runs title_step and in play runs frame_update
if joystick 1 is moved or fired clears the debounced key flags and skips the keyboard handling in this interrupt

loads the cave description, fills the cave with random objects, draws the steel border, builds the cave from its description, sets the play variables, zeroes the scroll speeds and draws the whole cave

starts a game: player 1 (zpa_9D = 0), clears the game-over flag zpa_A0, the six score digits zpf_5F-64 and the six digits to add zpf_4E-53, sets three men in zpa_5C, copies the first nine bytes of the player block (men, cave, level and score, zpa_5C-64) into both save areas, zpf_6B and zpf_7A, and takes player 1's high-score digits from zpf_74-79 into zpf_65-6A

takes a man from the current player, saves that player's state and, in a two-player game, switches to the other player when they still have men; sets the game-over flag zpa_A0 when nobody has any left
plays one rising run of notes on voice 3 for the end-of-cave bonus count
compares the six score digits with the high score digits and, when the score is higher, copies it over the high score
writes the two players' last scores and the high scores into the score lines at $9813-$9833 as characters
takes the next cave number from the order table at $81FE; at the end of a round ($15) goes back to cave A and raises the level, up to level 5

counts the time left into the score one second at a time: each second adds zpa_5E + 1 points, the level as the game shows it (1 to 5), with a blip (tally_blip), until low_time_check sets zpa_97 at a time of 000; then goes on to the next cave

updates the player's high score, then runs lose_life, which takes a man and in a two-player game may switch player; when the game is over (zpa_A0) sets the cave and level to 0, so program_entry shows the title next, and writes the score lines with format_score_lines

holds play (zpa_9B = 1, which stops the clock, the sound and the magic wall count); after a finished cave (zpa_9F) runs time_bonus_tally, which moves to the next cave, after an intermission (zpa_A6) goes to the next cave, otherwise runs end_player_turn; then, outside the demonstration (zpa_A2 = 0), rewrites the status line's characters for the player ($9855), the men ($9858, with E or A at $985B for MEN or MAN), the cave ($985E) and the level ($9860); clears zpa_94
the cave's main loop: runs update_pass again and again until a cave-ending state is set in zpa_97, then silences the sound, runs the end-of-cave actions and waits for the glisten effect to finish

plays the demonstration: reads the move script at $5EA8 a byte at a time, the joystick bits in the low four bits (into zpa_8B, which rockford_handler takes while zpa_A2 is set) and a repeat count in the high four bits, and runs one update pass per repeat; ends at a byte whose low four bits are zero (the $00 at $5EE7 ends the script) or when the fire button on port 1 is pressed ($6F0C); then silences the sound, runs end_of_cave_actions if Rockford reached the exit (zpa_9F), and sets the cave number zpa_5D to 0
copies the LAST and HIGH score text lines from $6F64 and $6F78 into $9812 and $9826, blanks the line at $983A and sets $983D to $3C

copies the graphics from where the program file holds them to where the VIC reads them: $5000-$53FF to $2000-$23FF (the text set and the two tables after it) and $5FE8-$63E7 to $3000-$33FF (the tile set); then from $8D46 zeroes the left 16 cells of bitmap rows 19 to 22 and copies the eight logo blocks $68E8-$6E67 into $37C0-$3F3F, the last six character rows of the bitmap at $2000 (the right 24 cells of rows 19 to 22 from $68E8, $69A8, $6A68 and $6B28, rows 23 and 24 whole from $6BE8 and $6D28); stores $FF in $3770-$3797 and 0 in $3798-$37BF, so sprite block $DE ($3780-$37BF) is eight solid lines and then empty; sets the sprite pointers of both screens ($0FF8, $2FF8) to $DE and the sprite colours to black, and puts sprites 0 to 6 side by side at y $3A, x from $17 in steps of $30, doubled in width: a black band across the screen

silences the sound and resets the key flags, scroll phases and positions, the cave and level (0), the animation phase, the flash and sound flags; sets zpa_CE to $FF and the logo flag zpa_A3, the demo flag zpa_A2 and zpa_CC to 1; the first time through (zpa_D5 not zero, cleared at $8E22) also blacks the border and background colours ($D020-$D024), sets the high-score digits zpf_65, zpf_74 and zpf_83 to the character 0, one player and one joystick (zpa_9E, zpa_A4, zpa_D0 = 1), clears zpa_A8 and the sparkle bytes, and runs init_score_lines and init_graphics
sets the screen buffer, loads the VIC table from $899C, switches on the raster interrupt at line $28 and points the interrupt vector at $8A0C

the program's real start, the target of the loader's jump and also of the RESTORE key's NMI vector: sets up the CIA timers that feed the random generator, the NMI vector, the banking, copies the two screen-copy templates from $7EF0 and $7FF0 to $9E00 and $9F00, loads the status line template and runs the title and game loop: with no cave chosen the title screen, otherwise sets up the cave, plays it (or the demo) and ends it

41 bytes that nothing refers to, after the program's last instruction (the BMI at $8F3B): part of an assembler's symbol table left in memory when the program was saved, in 12-byte entries, each a six-character ASCII name, $A8 $00, the label's value as a little-endian word and two flag bytes. $8F3D-$8F41 are the end of an entry whose value is $8A63 (b_8A63); then come 'KEY1  ' = $8A66 at $8F42 (j_8A66), ':SK3A ' = $8A74 at $8F4E (b_8A74) and ':SK4  ' = $8A84 at $8F5A (b_8A84), all places in raster_interrupt, the programmer's own names for them. The table runs on through asm_symbol_table_scrap at $8F66

1,024 bytes that nothing refers to.
